assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a designable chemical tool: bifunctional PROTACs and monovalent molecular glues (thalidomide-class drugs acting through cereblon) convert a biological phenomenon into a defined, rational chemical reaction at the protein surface. It created a general strategy for acting on proteins once considered undruggable and has reached clinical trials and approved molecular-glue drugs.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept (with Sakamoto) and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, making the molecular-glue mechanism chemically explicable. The credited list is large, so a three-person prize needs a clear split between PROTAC design and glue mechanism; Ciulli, Gray and others are real but would be excluded.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many labs and companies; mechanisms (ternary complex, ubiquitin transfer) are measured quantitatively. Clinical validation is growing but PROTAC drug approvals are still pending, so some of the clinical case is early. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Allocation among PROTAC originators, cereblon-mechanism discoverers and later degrader chemists is contested.
Clinical benefit of heterobifunctional degraders versus glues is not yet fully settled.
I rely on recalled literature and have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cytosine and adenine base editors convert deamination chemistry (engineered deaminases fused to a Cas9 nickase) into programmable single-nucleotide changes without double-strand breaks. It is a conceptually clear chemical mechanism applied to genome editing and has direct therapeutic relevance for correcting point mutations and for studying mutational mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led both editor classes; Komor and Gaudelli were the first authors who executed the decisive CBE and ABE work. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel, independent cytidine-deaminase system. A fair prize could be Liu alone or Liu with the two lead trainees; the Nobel tradition of senior-author credit favors Liu.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and in clinical use (first base-editing trials, patient treatments reported). The interpretation is stable; recognition is timely though the 2020 prize already honored CRISPR-Cas9, which may make a second genome-editing prize feel close.
uncertainties: Overlap with the separate prime-editing entry and with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Off-target deamination and bystander editing remain active concerns, though they do not undermine the principle.
Credit of Nishida/Kondo versus Komor/Gaudelli is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, built on nucleotide chemistry (reversible terminator nucleotides, pyrosequencing in picoliter reactors), reduced the cost of reading genomes by orders of magnitude and reshaped biology and medicine, including measurement of mutation spectra and replication-error signatures that bear on my own field. The impact is exceptional and the underlying chemistry is clear.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the reversible-terminator, single-molecule-cluster chemistry that underlies the dominant platform; Rothberg's group delivered the first commercial massively parallel pyrosequencing (454). Pascal Mayer's parallel idea and Jingyue Ju's terminator chemistry make attribution contestable, and platform engineering by companies complicates the picture.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of use, universal adoption, robust independent confirmation. Recognition is not premature; the question is whether it is late enough to be settled and which people to name.
uncertainties: Disputed allocation of credit among chemistry, enzymology and instrument engineering contributors.
Whether the committee prefers the chemistry core (terminators) to the platform inventors.
Facts on priority are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry for siRNA and mRNA medicines, including COVID-19 vaccines; the pH-dependent ionizable lipid design controls encapsulation, endosomal escape and tolerability. The impact is huge and tied to nucleic acid chemistry, though the 2023 Medicine prize recognized the nucleoside modifications rather than the delivery chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the foundational ionizable-lipid and LNP formulation work; MacLachlan contributed key siRNA-LNP development; Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries. The full credited list is large (also Madden, Hope), and industrial development is intertwined with academic work, so a fair three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale (patisiran, mRNA vaccines), with independent confirmation. Timing is arguably ideal after the pandemic, but the medicinal and formulation character may be viewed as better suited to Medicine.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse between academic and company-based inventors.
Chemistry-versus-medicine fit for the prize category.
Priority details recalled from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase converts N2 to ammonia with a unique FeMo-cofactor; structures of the MoFe protein and the cofactor's central carbide, together with kinetic and spectroscopic work on the E4 state, make this a fundamental chemical-mechanism problem with planetary and industrial significance. This is the kind of enzymology that interests me, though a final mechanism is not yet written.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first MoFe protein and FeMo-cofactor structures and the ligand-binding pictures, Einsle resolved the interstitial carbide and later structures, and Seefeldt contributed mechanistic kinetics. Dean, Ribbe and other biosynthetic and spectroscopic contributors are credited as well; Howard and Hoffman are not on the list, so a prize could omit relevant mechanistic workers.
assessment.maturity: Structural facts are well confirmed and independent. The catalytic mechanism and the N2 binding site are still under debate, which may make the recognition appear partly premature as a mechanism prize but secure as a structure prize.
uncertainties: Whether the N2 binding mode and the mechanism of reduction are sufficiently established.
Omission of key spectroscopy/mechanism researchers outside the credited names.
Facts from memory and not independently confirmed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic acid sequences electrically from single molecules through protein nanopores combines protein engineering, single-molecule measurement and chemistry, and enabled long-read sequencing, direct RNA sequencing and modified-base detection. It has delivered a new class of analytical instruments widely used in biology and public health.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brenner and Deamer showed DNA passes through alpha-hemolysin pores; Branton, Deamer and Akeson established the strand-sequencing principle; Bayley engineered pores and detection chemistry and founded the commercialization. This is a classical multi-person priority question with some very credible claimants.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a technology, independently validated, with increasing use; accuracy and application scope continue to improve. Recognition is timely, but a nanopore prize would compete with the sequencing field entry.
uncertainties: Multiple plausible claimants with unresolved priority between early proof of principle and engineering.
Overlap with the massively parallel sequencing entry.
Facts from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allow cells to incorporate designed amino acids, so the genetic code itself becomes chemically programmable. It opened new tools for studying enzymes and cell biology and for therapeutic protein design. The idea is clear and general and has been extensively reproduced.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the field with Wang (first in E. coli and then in eukaryotic systems), and Chin extended it to eukaryotes and to reprogrammed genomes and quadruplet codons. Mehl and Yokoyama provided important contributions that would be omitted, and the credit among Schultz-group members is not cleanly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely applied for two decades; independent labs reproduce the method. Applications are broad, though the sharpest therapeutic demonstration is more recent.
uncertainties: Credit split between Schultz/Wang and Chin is unresolved.
Whether the scientific breakthrough is judged to be the concept, the systems or the genome-wide recoding.
Details from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale mass spectrometric proteomics (shotgun methods, stable-isotope labeling, targeted and data-independent strategies) gave biologists a general tool to measure thousands of proteins and modifications, converting cellular regulation into quantitative chemistry. I value measurement tools of this kind, but the key conceptual step overlaps with the soft-ionization prize of 2002.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are plausible core figures, each tied to a distinct method class (SILAC/high-resolution workflows, ICAT and SRM, and MudPIT/shotgun). Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also credited, and instrument developers such as Makarov are separate entries. Allocation among a method and an instrument is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and cross-validated; proteomics is routine. Whether it is sufficiently novel relative to earlier MS prizes is a question, not one of maturity.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior mass spectrometry Nobel recognition (2002).
Contributions are divided among methods and instrument inventors.
Facts from memory.
